articles.title: ‘We live in grief-phobic societies’: experts on how to get more comfortable with death
articles.summary: We are all going to die, and so is everyone we know. So how can you not be terrified? For most people, death is not a standard conversation topic. Once, at lunch, a friend began talking about her mother’s death several years earlier.
body: Afterwards, I asked him what was wrong. “I really don’t like talking about death,” he said, his hands twitching anxiously. “I don’t even like thinking about it. It freaks me out.”
His discomfort struck me as silly – and also the most normal thing in the world. We are all going to die, and so is everyone we know. So why be terrified? And how can you not be terrified?

My friend is far from alone in his discomfort. “We live in grief-illiterate and grief-phobic societies,” says Dr Lucy Hone, a resilience and grief researcher and author of the book How Will I Get Ever Through This?: A Practical Guide to Navigating Life’s Toughest Times.

Hone began researching grief over a decade ago, after the sudden death of her daughter, Abi. On our video call, she wears one of Abi’s old hats, an orange and white beanie with polka dots and a big orange pouf on top. It’s ridiculous, Hone says, but it makes her laugh.

articles.summary: An unconventional technique makes this vibrant rice – finished with dill fronds – a lower-touch dinner for weeknights. Check out more Alice Zaslavsky recipes. This shortcut risotto will have purists shaking their fists, but I like to live dangerously.

articles.title: Who owns ‘brain rot’?: inside the international legal drama over a beloved meme
articles.summary: Copyright law in the US only applies to human-made creations, but AI characters like Tung Tung Tung Sahur are challenging that. One of the most beloved characters in an absurdist genre of online video content has become the center of an international legal battle that could determine where human…
body: Tung Tung Tung Sahur, also known as Triple T, was created in 2025 by an Indonesian teen who goes by the username Noxa, using OpenAI’s image-generation tool. Based on a kentongan – a type of drum used to wake south-east Asian Muslims for their pre-dawn meal during Ramadan – the character is an anthropomorphized version of the instrument with a broad smile and a vacant stare. He sits under the umbrella of “Italian brain rot” internet videos.

Since his creation, Triple T has become a global sensation: YouTube and TikTok host dozens of videos with hundreds of millions of views starring the character. People dress like Triple T at cosplay conventions and lovingly create fan art and animations of the stick-like creature, and his likeness appears on plushies, perfume and stickers.
The character has generated a great deal of money and stands to create much more – he will soon be joining Fortnite as a skin. But who should benefit from this virality?

Those microphones help power the active noise cancellation, Ambient Sound mode, and Adaptive Sound Control, so the headphones can respond to what's happening around you and automatically adjust how much outside sound gets through as your environment changes. There’s also plenty to tinker with in Sony’s companion app, including a customizable EQ for dialing in the sound to your preferences. Battery life is another reason the XM6 works well as an everyday pair—it can last up to 30 hours with ANC enabled and 40 hours with it switched off, although your actual runtime will vary depending on how you use them. That should comfortably cover a few days of commuting or work, as well as most long-haul flights. articles.title: The Tremendous Revival of Bangkok's Chao Phraya Waterfront
articles.summary: Tony Perrottet visits the banks of the Chao Phraya River, where old-school noodle stalls now share space with Michelin-starred restaurants and gilded temples soar over former warehouses turned art galleries.
body: “I bought this boat to explore the river's hidden places,” said Jern, a Bangkok interior designer whose full name is Irinrat Prasongchaikul, as we chugged in her vintage cruiser across the terra-cotta-colored waters of the Chao Phraya River, or River of Kings. She had invited me to join her and a half-dozen local friends for a sunset spin on her romantic vessel, which was built in 1957 but whose polished-wood deck shaded by a canopy felt like a throwback to the colonial-era seafaring days of Joseph Conrad. The boatman soon steered us past the majestic Wat Arun (Temple of Dawn) to Thonburi, the less-frequented western side of the waterway, then navigated into a dreamy klong, or canal.
“I grew up in Bangkok knowing that the Chao Phraya was important,” Jern added, popping open an iced bottle of Champagne. “But there's so much that has been forgotten.”

Water in every form is revered in Thailand, Jern explained, and the Chao Phraya has special status. “As a Thai,” she said, “I was always taught to respect the water goddess, Phra Mae Khongkha, who is associated with purification and fertility. We are taught that we can live without electricity, but water is our first resource.”

articles.summary: In Condé Nast Traveler's November issue, we reveal readers' favorite hotels, resorts, airlines, spas, and more—plus, the continent that just keeps getting more popular.
body: There are certain travel trends you can feel before you see them in the numbers. This year the message from our Readers' Choice Awards is remarkably clear: Asia is more enticing than ever.

Japan, of course, has been booming since the pandemic. I traveled there for the first time only last year and was lucky enough to be in Osaka and Kyoto the week the cherry blossoms were in full bloom. I rode an e-bike early in the mornings as the first rays of the sun started to illuminate Kyoto, and I'd stop every so often just to take in the beauty of the flowers up close, in complete solitude before the crowds arrived. It remains one of my most enchanting travel memories.

articles.title: Olivia Rodrigo’s Fall Style? Call It Boho-Grunge
articles.summary: The singer stepped out on a chilly New York day wearing an intriguing combo of pieces.
body: One A-lister who’s already on board with autumnal dressing? That would be Olivia Rodrigo. Earlier today, the singer—who is currently on her Unraveled Tour—stepped out in the city to run some errands on her day off. And as usual, she served up some serious cool-girl styling.

Rodrigo wore layered a black knit shawl sweater over a striped long-sleeve tee, and then she paired it with a pleated knee skirt and leather biker boots. Don’t forget her Supervinyl hat, too—an ode to the popular Hollywood record store.

There’s something intriguing about this particular combo of pieces in her outfit. It’s all slightly free-spirited—thanks to the off-the-shoulder shawl and swishy skirt—yet slightly edgy too, thanks to those chunky below-the-knee boots. It’s a signature Rodrigo approach to dressing, of course: The singer always balanced sweet-yet-tough elements in her ensembles. One minute, she’s in retro babydoll dresses, and the next she’ll rock cool vintage punk tees.

articles.title: Kraft Mac & Cheese Is Quietly Launching a New Type of Noodle
articles.summary: A box of mac and cheese is always a good thing to have tucked away in a cabinet for “emergencies.” Whether that occasion is not wanting to cook dinner or needing an easy late-night snack, mac and cheese is always a good idea. My brand of choice is Kraft Mac & Cheese.
body: Another thing I like to keep stocked in my pantry (for similar reasons) is ramen noodles. So when I heard that Kraft was launching cheesy ramen noodles, I was intrigued. Two of my favorite comfort foods merged into one? Yes, please! Here’s what we know about the upcoming drop.

According to snack account @snackolator, Kraft Mac & Cheese is bringing three cheesy ramen noodle flavors to U.S. stores in April 2027: spicy, chicken, and pork. Each pack promises “cheesy goodness” in just 3 1/2 minutes.

This will be Kraft’s first time entering a new category in 20 years. According to the brand, cheesy ramen has emerged as one of the biggest ramen categories in recent years, so consumers will hopefully be extremely excited to see Kraft’s spin on it.
